content: 1. Amlodipine and benazepril are combined in a medication approved by the FDA for the treatment of hypertension. Amlodipine is a dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker (DHP CCB), while benazepril is an angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitor. 2. WikiDoc provides educational content based on FDA package inserts, the National Library of Medicine, and clinical guidelines but does not replace professional healthcare advice or guarantee the validity of its information. 3. WikiDoc does not endorse the use of any medication or device in a manner inconsistent with its labeling. 4. The initial recommended dose of Lotrel (amlodipine/benazepril) is one capsule containing amlodipine 2.5 mg and benazepril 10 mg, taken orally once daily. 5. The antihypertensive effects of Lotrel are generally achieved within two weeks. 6. Amlodipine is effective in doses of 2.5–10 mg daily, while benazepril is effective in doses of 10–80 mg daily. Clinical trials have shown that increasing doses of amlodipine and benazepril in combination therapy enhances antihypertensive effects, particularly in non-Black patients. 7. Lotrel is contraindicated in patients with a history of angioedema, hypersensitivity to benazepril, amlodipine, or any of its excipients, and in patients with diabetes who are taking aliskiren. 8. ACE inhibitors, including benazepril, may cause angioedema, which can involve the face, extremities, lips, tongue, glottis, or larynx. Laryngeal edema can be fatal. If symptoms occur, discontinue Lotrel immediately and provide appropriate treatment, such as subcutaneous epinephrine. 9. Intestinal angioedema has been reported in patients on ACE inhibitors, presenting with abdominal pain, nausea, or vomiting. Diagnosis may require imaging or surgery, and symptoms typically resolve after discontinuation of the ACE inhibitor. 10. ACE inhibitors may cause anaphylactoid reactions during desensitization therapy or dialysis with high-flux membranes. Temporary discontinuation of the ACE inhibitor can prevent these reactions. 11. Amlodipine may cause worsening angina or acute myocardial infarction, particularly in patients with severe obstructive coronary artery disease, when therapy is initiated or the dose is increased. 12. Lotrel can cause symptomatic hypotension, especially in patients who are volumeor salt-depleted due to diuretics, dietary restrictions, dialysis, diarrhea, or vomiting. Volume and salt depletion should be corrected before starting therapy. 13. Use of ACE inhibitors during the second and third trimesters of pregnancy can cause fetal renal dysfunction, oligohydramnios, lung hypoplasia, skeletal deformities, and neonatal complications such as anuria, hypotension, and death. Lotrel should be discontinued as soon as pregnancy is detected. 14. Rare cases of cholestatic hepatitis and acute liver failure, some fatal, have been reported with ACE inhibitors. Patients developing jaundice or significant liver enzyme elevations should discontinue the drug and be monitored closely. 15. Renal function should be monitored periodically in patients on Lotrel, as ACE inhibitors can cause acute renal failure, particularly in patients with renal artery stenosis, severe heart failure, or volume depletion. 16. Hyperkalemia may occur in patients on Lotrel, especially those with renal insufficiency, diabetes, or concurrent use of potassium-sparing diuretics, potassium supplements, or potassium-containing salt substitutes. Serum potassium levels should be monitored regularly. 17. Persistent nonproductive cough has been reported with ACE inhibitors, likely due to inhibition of bradykinin degradation. The cough typically resolves after discontinuation of therapy. 18. The dose of simvastatin should not exceed 20 mg daily in patients on amlodipine. 19. 20. Initial doses of Lotrel should be lower, and patients should be monitored for greater sensitivity to the drug. 21. Overdose of amlodipine has been reported in a few cases, with symptoms ranging from asymptomatic to refractory shock and death. Management of overdose should include intensive care and symptomatic treatment. 22. 23. Minimal amounts of benazepril and its active metabolite are excreted into breast milk. Nursing mothers should either discontinue the drug or stop breastfeeding. 24. There is limited information on the use of Lotrel in pediatric patients, and its safety and efficacy in this population have not been established. 25.
